runs.content: Saturday full sweep — skimmed the overview/index page of every domain instead of deep-reading one, biasing toward cross-domain connections. A quiet day operationally: email-to-clipping failed (Gmail OAuth token expired/revoked, invalid_grant on search_emails and list_email_labels — needs manual re-auth, not a wiki-thinker fix), and recipe-recommender's weekly batch drew on the same three chefs (Chang, Bourdain, Slater) as every recent run. The only genuinely new source material was today's podcast-summarizer catch-up (4 pages: Prof G Markets on Meta's AI data moat, a David Gardner/Motley Fool interview, and two CyberHack: The Conti Files episodes). Found one real connection: podcasts/podcast-behind-the-balance-sheet-the-fool-david-gardner.md has Gardner stating his core investing heuristics directly — he leans into stocks critics call 'grossly overvalued,' and his best stock-picking rule is buying the top dog/first mover in an emerging industry regardless of price. finance/ideas/idea-ge-vernova.md and finance/ideas/idea-bloom-energy.md each independently describe businesses that fit those exact criteria (GEV explicitly trades '55% above what bullish analysts think it's worth'; Bloom Energy's own scorecard says 'zero margin of safety... traditional value investors should not own this stock') — but both pages read those same facts purely through a single Berkshire-style margin-of-safety lens and land on 'Watch, wait for a pullback,' never engaging the alternative growth-investing framework Gardner represents, where the 'overvalued' consensus is the buy signal, not the reason to wait. Concrete next step: add a line to both idea pages' Verdict sections naming Gardner's framework as the explicit alternative lens being declined, cross-linked from the podcast page. Checked the open sections for resolution: nothing showed clear signs of being actioned since 2026-09-25.

Friday's rotation deep-dives Lightfin + Games + Cooking + Sports Betting + Work. All five are extremely stale — Lightfin unchanged since the finale-outline note, Games' prototypes.md still an unpopulated placeholder since 2026-05-01, Sports Betting still a scaffold, Work has had exactly one source page since 2026-05-15. The only new material anywhere in this group today was the recipe-recommender's weekly batch (week of 2026-09-28) — same three chefs (Chang, Bourdain, Slater) as every recent batch, nothing new to connect. Widened the search to the whole wiki map instead of requiring fresh source material, and found one real gap: work/overview.md's own Key Platforms table names 'SAP SuccessFactors' as the legacy HCM incumbent at the center of the domain's whole organising thread (the 'Workday Last Workday' AI-native-disruption debate) — but nothing on that page notes that Fred actually holds SAP SE as a real, live trading-portfolio position (17 shares, +33.37% unrealised, 5.21% weight). finance/source-sap-prior-labs-2026.md gives SAP a full investment write-up, but purely as an enterprise-AI/tabular-foundation-model thesis — it never mentions the SuccessFactors business or the disruption debate at all. Fred has real capital riding on the 'incumbent adapts' side of a question Work's whole domain exists to track, and neither page notices. Concrete next step: add a row to work/overview.md's Key Platforms table flagging SAP as a live holding (cross-linked to finance/trading-portfolio.md), and add a line to source-sap-prior-labs-2026.md's thesis citing the SuccessFactors/Workday disruption debate as a business-line risk the pure enterprise-AI read doesn't capture.
